For EACH finding: use WebSearch/WebFetch (load via ToolSearch with query "select:WebSearch,WebFetch" if needed) to confirm the named standard/framework/tool/paper actually exists and that "what_it_defines" and "form_elements" accurately describe it. [{"name":"LLM-as-a-judge foundational research (MT-Bench, Zheng et al. 2023)","tradition":"ML evaluation research","source_type":"paper","citation":"Zheng, L. et al., \"Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena,\" NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks Track (arXiv:2306.05685)","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.05685","what_it_defines":"Establishes that strong LLMs grading open-ended output can reach high agreement with human preference (~80%+ with GPT-4 on MT-Bench), and names the canonical judge failure modes: position bias (favoring an answer by placement), verbosity bias (favoring longer answers), self-enhancement bias (favoring the judge's own model family), and limited reasoning ability on math/logic. Proposes mitigations: swapping positions, few-shot judging, reference-guided grading, chain-of-thought.","form_elements":["Pairwise comparison vs. single-answer grading as two judge modes","Position-swap to detect/cancel position bias","Reference-guided judging (give the judge a reference answer)","Chain-of-thought before verdict","Agreement-with-human measurement as the meta-metric for judge quality"],"fit_notes":"This is the evidence base any LLM-judged fitness-test layer must be designed against, not a format to adopt. For the shop's seed layer it dictates derived-check design rules: use single-output grading against explicit criteria (not pairwise, which imports position bias), prefer a different model family for judging than generating (self-preference), instruct the judge that length/effort is not merit (verbosity), and require reasoning-before-verdict. These rules belong in the judge-role definition that gets compiled into the reviewing agent's context.","adopt_potential":"context-only"},{"name":"Judge gameability: null-model benchmark cheating (ICLR 2025)","tradition":"ML evaluation research / adversarial robustness","source_type":"paper","citation":"Zheng, X. et al., \"Cheating Automatic LLM Benchmarks: Null Models Achieve High Win Rates,\" ICLR 2025 Oral (arXiv:2410.07137)","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.07137","what_it_defines":"Demonstrates that a null model emitting a constant, input-irrelevant adversarial response achieves top-ranked win rates on judge-scored benchmarks (86.5% LC win rate on AlpacaEval 2.0, 83.0 on Arena-Hard-Auto, 9.55 on MT-Bench), proving LLM judges are structurally gameable by output that manipulates the grading prompt rather than doing the task. Calls for anti-cheating mechanisms in automatic evaluation.","form_elements":["Adversarial constant-output attack on judge prompts","Transferability of cheating outputs across unseen test instructions","Anti-cheating requirement as a design constraint for judge pipelines"],"fit_notes":"Directly relevant threat model for the shop: the generating agent and the judging agent are both LLMs inside one system, so Goodharting is a live risk — a generator optimized (even implicitly, via retry loops) against a known rubric can learn to satisfy the judge without satisfying the intent. Mitigations for the derived-check layer: keep judge prompts/rubrics out of the generator's context where feasible, delimit and label the evaluated artifact as untrusted data in the judge prompt, spot-audit judge verdicts with human review, and never treat judge pass-rate as the sole gate for high-stakes artifacts.","adopt_potential":"context-only"},{"name":"G-Eval criteria-to-steps judging procedure","tradition":"NLG evaluation research (implemented in DeepEval)","source_type":"paper","citation":"Liu, Y. et al., \"G-Eval: NLG Evaluation using GPT-4 with Better Human Alignment,\" EMNLP 2023, pp. 2511–2522 (arXiv:2303.16634); productionized as DeepEval's GEval metric","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.16634","what_it_defines":"The canonical procedure for turning a short natural-language quality criterion into a reproducible LLM grading run: (1) the judge LLM auto-expands the criterion into explicit chain-of-thought evaluation steps, (2) grades via a form-filling paradigm against those steps, (3) optionally weights the score by output-token probabilities for finer granularity. Achieved the then-best human correlation on summarization quality (Spearman 0.514).","form_elements":["criteria: one-paragraph plain-language quality definition","evaluation_steps: enumerated checks derived from the criteria (auto-generated or hand-fixed)","evaluation_params: which artifact fields the judge sees (input, output, context, reference)","1–N scale score with threshold, plus judge reason"],"fit_notes":"Strong structural fit with the shop's founding principle that checks are DERIVED from construction definitions: G-Eval is literally a derivation procedure (definition → evaluation steps → grade). For the seed layer, the criteria + fixed evaluation_steps pair is an adoptable micro-format for each fitness test regardless of execution framework; hand-pinning the evaluation steps (rather than letting the judge re-derive them per run) trades a little alignment for determinism and auditability, which suits a quality layer that must be reviewable.","adopt_potential":"adapt"},{"name":"EvalGen / criteria drift (Who Validates the Validators)","tradition":"HCI + ML evaluation research","source_type":"paper","citation":"Shankar, S. et al., \"Who Validates the Validators? Aligning LLM-Assisted Evaluation of LLM Outputs with Human Preferences,\" UIST 2024 (arXiv:2404.12272)","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.12272","what_it_defines":"A mixed-initiative workflow (EvalGen) for authoring evaluation criteria and their implementations (code assertions or LLM-judge prompts), selecting implementations by alignment with human grades on sampled outputs. Its central empirical finding is criteria drift: humans need to grade outputs to discover their criteria, so evaluation criteria cannot be fully specified a priori and are partially dependent on the outputs observed.","form_elements":["Criteria list authored per task, each implemented as code assertion or judge prompt","Human grading of sampled outputs as alignment signal","Implementation selection by agreement with human grades","Iterative criteria revision as outputs are observed"],"fit_notes":"Two direct consequences for the shop's seed layer. First, the fitness-test sets must be versioned living artifacts with an explicit revision loop fed by human (product-authority) spot-grading — a static fire-and-forget test set contradicts the criteria-drift evidence. Second, it legitimizes the 'small set' framing in the proposal: EvalGen-style practice starts from a handful of criteria and grows them from observed failures, not from exhaustive upfront enumeration. The full EvalGen tooling is not needed; the calibration loop is the adaptable practice.","adopt_potential":"adapt"},{"name":"promptfoo declarative rubric assertions and scenarios","tradition":"Production LLM eval tooling (open source)","source_type":"tool","citation":"promptfoo documentation: model-graded metrics, llm-rubric assertion, and scenarios config (promptfoo/promptfoo on GitHub)","url":"https://www.promptfoo.dev/docs/configuration/expected-outputs/model-graded/llm-rubric/","what_it_defines":"A declarative YAML eval format: test cases carry vars (inputs/context) and assert blocks; the llm-rubric assertion type states a plain-language expected property ('is concise and apologetic', 'does not invent facts') that a grader model scores, returning pass/score/reason. The scenarios construct groups shared data (config: vars sets) with a set of tests run against each — a matrix of context × expectations. Also ships g-eval, factuality, select-best, and classifier assertions.","form_elements":["tests[].vars — the Given/When analog (input and context)","tests[].assert[] with type: llm-rubric and value: <natural-language criterion> — the Then analog","scenarios[] — config (vars sets) crossed with tests","Grader provider pinning and per-assertion thresholds","Assertions co-resident with deterministic checks (regex, json, contains) in one file"],"fit_notes":"The closest established, adoptable FORMAT to what the shop needs: it already is 'scenario + natural-language fitness assertions judged by an LLM, alongside mechanical checks' in a stable, documented, widely-used YAML form. The vars/assert structure is semantically isomorphic to Given-When/Then. Adopting promptfoo's format (or its schema as the interchange shape) would satisfy the strong-preference-for-established-forms rule; the shop's Gherkin surface could compile down to it. Caveat: the format is tool-coupled and per-test-case, not artifact-type-schema-aware — it would sit at the derived-check layer, not the definition layer.","adopt_potential":"adopt"},{"name":"DeepEval G-Eval metric implementation","tradition":"Production LLM eval tooling (open source)","source_type":"tool","citation":"DeepEval documentation, \"G-Eval\" metric (Confident AI / deepeval)","url":"https://deepeval.com/docs/metrics-llm-evals","what_it_defines":"Pytest-style Python eval framework whose GEval metric implements the G-Eval paper for arbitrary custom criteria: define criteria or explicit evaluation_steps, select evaluation_params (input/actual output/expected output/context), get a probability-weighted 0–1 score with threshold and reason. Positioned as the framework's most versatile metric for any custom qualitative dimension.","form_elements":["LLMTestCase: input, actual_output, expected_output, retrieval_context","GEval(criteria=... | evaluation_steps=[...], threshold=...)","Score + reason output per test case","CI integration via pytest-style assertions"],"fit_notes":"Confirms the criteria/evaluation_steps pair as a de facto industry micro-format (same shape as the paper). Less attractive than promptfoo as a FORMAT for the shop because the definition lives in Python code rather than declarative artifact files — the shop's seed layer wants tool-independent definitional documents. Useful as an execution backend or as schema inspiration for the fitness-test document type.","adopt_potential":"adapt"},{"name":"Ragas rubric-based scoring and AspectCritique","tradition":"Production LLM eval tooling (open source, RAG-origin)","source_type":"tool","citation":"Ragas documentation: Rubric-Based Evaluation and Aspect Critique metrics","url":"https://docs.ragas.io/en/latest/concepts/metrics/available_metrics/rubrics_based/","what_it_defines":"Two reusable judged-metric shapes: (a) rubric-based scoring — a score-anchored rubric with a written description per score level (1–5), used for domain-specific quality; (b) AspectCritique — binary yes/no judgment against a single named aspect (harmfulness, conciseness, or user-defined criteria). Plus the RAG-specific judged metrics (faithfulness, answer relevance, context precision/recall) it popularized.","form_elements":["Score-anchored rubric: explicit description for each score level","Binary aspect critique: one aspect, one yes/no criterion","Component-wise metric decomposition (faithfulness vs relevance vs context quality)"],"fit_notes":"The score-anchored rubric (a written description per level, not just a bare 1–5 scale) is the established form the shop should use anywhere a graded rather than binary verdict is wanted — bare Likert scales without level descriptions are known to judge inconsistently. The binary aspect-critique shape maps naturally onto a single Then-clause. Ragas as a tool is RAG-centric and not otherwise a fit.","adopt_potential":"adapt"},{"name":"LangSmith / OpenEvals judge evaluators","tradition":"Production LLM eval tooling (LangChain ecosystem)","source_type":"tool","citation":"LangChain, openevals library and LangSmith evaluation docs (\"Evaluating Large Language Models With OpenEvals\"; LangSmith evaluation concepts)","url":"https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/evaluation-concepts","what_it_defines":"Prebuilt and factory-built LLM-as-judge evaluators (correctness, conciseness, helpfulness, plus custom rubric prompts) run against datasets of examples or live traces; documented authoring guidance: state exactly what constitutes good/bad, choose binary over continuous where possible, include few-shot examples of good and bad outputs, allow custom output schemas.","form_elements":["Dataset of examples (input, optional reference output)","Judge prompt template with rubric and few-shot good/bad exemplars","Binary-preferred scoring guidance","Offline (dataset) vs online (trace) evaluation split"],"fit_notes":"Its authoring guidance (binary-preferred verdicts, exemplar-anchored rubrics) matches the rest of the field and should inform the shop's content-quality-guideline format. As tooling it is platform-coupled (LangSmith) and adds no format element promptfoo/DeepEval don't already provide; survey-level context rather than an adoption candidate.","adopt_potential":"context-only"},{"name":"Braintrust autoevals scorer library","tradition":"Production LLM eval tooling (commercial + OSS library)","source_type":"tool","citation":"Braintrust, autoevals library (braintrustdata/autoevals on GitHub) and \"LLM-as-a-judge scorers and classifiers\" docs","url":"https://github.com/braintrustdata/autoevals","what_it_defines":"Open-source library of preconfigured LLM-judge scorers (Factuality, ClosedQA, Summarization, etc.) and the LLMClassifierFromTemplate pattern: a judge prompt plus an explicit choice→score mapping (e.g., A=1.0, B=0.5, C=0.0), which forces the judge into a constrained classification rather than freeform scoring; scores normalized 0–100%.","form_elements":["Choice-based classification with explicit choice_scores mapping","Prompt-template scorer definition (portable, YAML-representable)","Code scorers and judge scorers under one scorer interface"],"fit_notes":"The choice→score mapping (constrained enumeration of verdict options with defined meanings) is a judge-reliability technique worth folding into the shop's judge-prompt conventions — it reduces scoring variance versus asking for a free 1–10. Otherwise ecosystem-redundant with promptfoo/DeepEval for the shop's purposes.","adopt_potential":"context-only"},{"name":"OpenAI evals framework and eval design guidance","tradition":"Model-provider eval tooling and guidance","source_type":"framework","citation":"OpenAI, evals framework (openai/evals on GitHub: build-eval.md, model-graded eval templates in JSON/YAML registry) and \"Evaluation best practices\" developer guide","url":"https://github.com/openai/evals","what_it_defines":"The original open registry format for evals: JSONL datasets plus YAML eval definitions; model-graded templates (fact, closedqa, battle) where a judge model compares output to ideal answers or grades against a criterion — the direct ancestor of promptfoo's model-graded assertions. The developer-platform guidance covers designing graders and eval-driven development. Note: the hosted Evals platform is being deprecated (read-only Oct 2026, shutdown Nov 2026); the open-source repo and the guidance remain the citable prior art.","form_elements":["JSONL sample format (input, ideal)","YAML eval registry entry (eval class + args + dataset ref)","Model-graded template: prompt with {output} and {criteria}/{ideal} slots, constrained verdict choices","Two-stage answer-then-judge flow"],"fit_notes":"Historically important as the form most later tools copied; the model-graded template with constrained verdict choices is the same micro-format as Braintrust's classifier and promptfoo's rubric. Given the hosted platform's deprecation and the repo's benchmark-registry orientation, it is prior-art context and format precedent rather than an adoption target.","adopt_potential":"context-only"},{"name":"Anthropic eval-writing guidance","tradition":"Model-provider guidance","source_type":"practice","citation":"Anthropic, \"Define success criteria and build evaluations\" (Claude platform docs) and \"Demystifying evals for AI agents\" (Anthropic engineering blog)","url":"https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents","what_it_defines":"Provider-canonical practice for eval authoring: SMART-style success criteria; design principles (task-specific with edge cases; automate when possible; prefer volume of lower-signal automated grading over few hand-graded items); a grader hierarchy — deterministic/code-based where possible, LLM graders where necessary, humans judiciously for calibration; LLM-grading mechanics (different model for judging than generating, one isolated judge per quality dimension, constrained output like 'output only the number', defined scale anchors, allow 'Unknown', frequent calibration against expert human judgment).","form_elements":["Success-criteria statement format (specific, measurable, achievable, relevant)","Grader hierarchy: code-based → LLM-based → human","One-dimension-per-judge isolation rule","Likert/binary/ordinal grading prompt patterns with anchored scales","Calibration loop against human judgment"],"fit_notes":"Directly adoptable as the authoring standard for the shop's fitness-test sets and the judge conventions derived from them: the grader hierarchy operationalizes 'mechanical checks first, LLM rubric only for what code cannot check', which matches the shop's definitions-precede-checks principle, and the one-dimension-per-judge rule dictates that a multi-clause fitness set be judged clause-by-clause, not holistically. This is guidance to encode into role/skill definitions, not a file format.","adopt_potential":"adopt"},{"name":"CheckList behavioral testing methodology","tradition":"NLP testing research (pre-LLM-judge)","source_type":"paper","citation":"Ribeiro, M.T., Wu, T., Guestrin, C., Singh, S., \"Beyond Accuracy: Behavioral Testing of NLP Models with CheckList,\" ACL 2020 Best Paper (arXiv:2005.04118)","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.04118","what_it_defines":"A task-agnostic behavioral-testing methodology for NLP systems borrowed from software behavioral testing: a matrix of linguistic capabilities × three test types — Minimum Functionality Tests (small targeted unit-like probes), Invariance tests (perturbations that must not change output), and Directional expectation tests (perturbations that must change output a known way). Empirically, practitioners with CheckList wrote 2x the tests and found ~3x the bugs.","form_elements":["Capability × test-type matrix for test ideation","MFT: minimal targeted probe with expected behavior","INV: perturbation + output-invariance expectation","DIR: perturbation + expected direction of change","Template-based case generation for coverage"],"fit_notes":"The strongest pre-LLM precedent for the proposal's 'small set of targeted qualitative tests' framing: MFTs are exactly small behavioral probes rather than exhaustive suites, and the capability×test-type matrix is a disciplined ideation device the shop can reuse when deriving fitness sets from construction definitions. INV/DIR test types translate to LLM-judged form (e.g., 'restating the brief in different words must not change the verdict'). Methodology to adapt; the tooling itself targets classifier-era NLP.","adopt_potential":"adapt"},{"name":"Giskard agent testing and scan","tradition":"ML/LLM quality-assurance tooling (open source + platform)","source_type":"tool","citation":"Giskard-AI/giskard-oss (GitHub) and Giskard documentation: LLM scan, test suites, agent evaluation","url":"https://docs.giskard.ai/","what_it_defines":"An evaluation/testing library for ML models and LLM agents: automated scan generating adversarial test suites from a plain-language agent description (prompt injection, harmful content, hallucination, robustness classes), plus persistent domain test suites for regression testing agent behavior across versions, combining heuristic and LLM-assisted detectors.","form_elements":["Plain-language agent description as scan seed","Vulnerability-class taxonomy (hallucination, injection, bias, robustness, disclosure)","Persistent test suite object re-run across model/agent versions","Heuristic + LLM-judge detector pairing"],"fit_notes":"Despite occasionally being described alongside BDD, Giskard is not a Given-When-Then framework — its relevance is the pattern of deriving a test suite from a natural-language behavior description (cousin to the shop's derive-checks-from-definitions principle) and its vulnerability-class taxonomy, useful when the fitness sets must cover robustness/safety dimensions, not just content quality. Context and taxonomy source, not a format to adopt.","adopt_potential":"context-only"},{"name":"LangWatch Scenario: simulation-based agent testing with judge agent","tradition":"Agent testing tooling (open source)","source_type":"tool","citation":"langwatch/scenario (GitHub) — \"Agentic testing for agentic codebases\"; LangWatch agent-simulation docs","url":"https://github.com/langwatch/scenario","what_it_defines":"An agent-testing framework where each test is a named scenario: a described situation, a simulated user driving a multi-turn interaction, and a Judge Agent holding a list of plain-language criteria that it evaluates at every turn, deciding pass/fail/continue. Scenarios run in CI. This is the closest living implementation of 'scenario-shaped test whose assertions are natural-language criteria evaluated by an LLM rather than executed as code'.","form_elements":["Scenario: name + situation description (Given/When analog)","criteria: [list of natural-language expectations] (Then analog)","JudgeAgent evaluating criteria per turn with verdict + reasoning","UserSimulatorAgent for multi-turn drive","CI-runnable script per scenario"],"fit_notes":"Direct prior art for the product authority's proposal minus the Gherkin keywords: it demonstrates the pattern is viable and shipping in an established OSS tool, and its structure (situation + criteria list + judge) is exactly what a judged Gherkin scenario compiles to. For the shop, its multi-turn user simulation is more machinery than the artifact-fitness use case needs, but its scenario/criteria/judge schema is the strongest external validation that the proposed form works. Adapt: borrow the schema semantics, keep the shop's Gherkin surface syntax.","adopt_potential":"adapt"},{"name":"BDD-for-AI prior art: LLMs and Gherkin intersect in the other direction","tradition":"Software engineering research (BDD × LLM)","source_type":"paper","citation":"Representative primary sources: \"Comprehensive Evaluation and Insights into the Use of LLMs in the Automation of BDD Acceptance Test Formulation\" (arXiv:2403.14965); \"From Law to Gherkin\" (arXiv:2508.20744); \"Epic-Organized vs. Requirement-Aligned Gherkin: An Empirical Evaluation of LLM-Based Acceptance Criteria Generation\" (SEET 2026, arXiv:2607.01980); LLM-as-a-Judge rubric evaluation of Gherkin artifacts (arXiv:2512.01232)","url":"https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.14965","what_it_defines":"The published BDD×LLM literature covers: LLMs generating Gherkin scenarios from requirements/regulations; empirical quality evaluation of that generated Gherkin (including rubric-driven LLM-as-judge assessment of scenario completeness, criteria alignment, and assertion quality); and classic executable BDD (Cucumber/behave step definitions). What it does NOT contain is an established, named standard for the inverse pattern — authoring G/W/T scenarios as fitness specifications for LLM output and having an LLM judge (rather than step-definition code) evaluate the Then-clauses. That exact pattern exists only as near-neighbors (LangWatch Scenario's criteria lists, promptfoo's rubric assertions) and scattered experiments.","form_elements":["Gherkin G/W/T as LLM-parseable and LLM-generatable structure (empirically supported)","Rubric dimensions used when LLMs judge Gherkin quality: completeness, criteria alignment, assertion specificity","Executable-BDD convention: every step binds to a step definition (the cultural default the proposal breaks)"],"fit_notes":"Establishes two things for the proposal assessment: (1) Gherkin's structured natural language is demonstrably friendly to LLM consumption, supporting the reuse-one-literacy argument; (2) there is no external standard to simply adopt for judge-evaluated Gherkin, so that specific combination is bespoke and needs the justification the shop's rules demand — the justification available is that it is a thin syntax layer over the well-established scenario+criteria+judge pattern. Also flags the cultural risk: in every established Gherkin ecosystem, scenarios are assumed executable, so judged-not-executed features need unmistakable marking.","adopt_potential":"context-only"},{"name":"Gherkin-as-qualitative-fitness proposal","tradition":"Internal proposal (shopsystem product authority), assessed against external evidence","source_type":"practice","citation":"Product authority proposal (verbatim, internal): \"Use Given/When/Then Gherkin/BDD form tests to establish fitness... as long as it is understood they won't be backed by typical code-style implementation... at least a small set of tests to evaluate fitness of any given generated output.\" Assessed against: LangWatch Scenario (github.com/langwatch/scenario), promptfoo llm-rubric/scenarios (promptfoo.dev), G-Eval (arXiv:2303.16634), Zheng et al. (arXiv:2306.05685), null-model cheating (arXiv:2410.07137), EvalGen criteria drift (arXiv:2404.12272), Anthropic eval guidance (anthropic.com/engineering/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents), CheckList (arXiv:2005.04118)","url":"https://github.com/langwatch/scenario","what_it_defines":"Proposal: express qualitative fitness tests for non-deterministic LLM-generated output as Given/When/Then Gherkin scenarios, explicitly NOT backed by executable step definitions — evaluated instead by an LLM reviewer — with a small (not extensive) set per generated-output type.","form_elements":["Feature file per artifact/output type, tagged non-executable (e.g., @judged / kept outside executable features/ tree)","Given = artifact context and inputs available to the judge; When = the generation activity under test; Then/And = one falsifiable, observable quality property per clause","Per-clause binary verdict + judge reasoning (one dimension per judgment, per Anthropic guidance)","Compilation target: each Then-clause maps 1:1 to a rubric assertion (promptfoo llm-rubric / criteria-list entry / G-Eval evaluation step)","Calibration record: periodic human (product-authority) grading of sampled verdicts per EvalGen criteria-drift finding"],"fit_notes":"VERDICT: ADAPT — sound pattern, bespoke surface syntax, adoptable with guardrails. PRIOR ART: the exact combination (Gherkin syntax + LLM judge instead of step definitions) has no established named standard — BDD×LLM literature runs the other direction (LLMs generating/assessing Gherkin). But the underlying semantics are firmly established: LangWatch Scenario ships scenario-shaped tests whose assertions are plain-language criteria evaluated by a Judge Agent; promptfoo's scenarios+llm-rubric YAML is structurally isomorphic (vars=Given/When, rubric assertion=Then); G-Eval canonizes criteria→steps→judged-score. So the proposal is a thin syntax adaptation of orthodox practice, which satisfies the shop's bespoke-requires-justification bar: the justification is literacy reuse — Gherkin is already this shop's behavior-contract vocabulary (features/ tree, scenario hashes, assign_scenarios), so PO-authored fitness tests need no second formalism, and the research above confirms G/W/T is LLM-friendly structure. STRENGTHS: (1) single authoring literacy across behavior contracts and fitness tests; (2) G/W/T forces context (Given) and activity (When) to be explicit, which judge prompts need anyway; (3) one-clause-one-property structure aligns with Anthropic's isolated-dimension judging rule; (4) 'small set' matches CheckList MFT practice and EvalGen's grow-from-observed-failures finding — small is the established norm for qualitative sets, not a compromise. FAILURE MODES: (1) unfalsifiable Then-clauses ('Then the brief is compelling') — the judge will happily pass vibes; mitigation: authoring rule that every Then names an observable property whose violation a reviewer could point at, plus score-anchored or binary phrasing (Ragas rubric form, Braintrust choice_scores); (2) judge gameability/Goodharting (null-model result, self-preference, verbosity bias) — mitigation: judge model/context separated from generator, artifact delimited as untrusted data, reasoning-before-verdict, spot-audits by human; (3) executable-culture confusion — every established Gherkin ecosystem assumes step definitions exist, so judged features WILL eventually be fed to a runner or 'fixed' by an agent that binds steps; mitigation: hard segregation (distinct directory such as fitness/ not features/, mandatory tag, header comment stating evaluation semantics) and a schema-level marker in the artifact-type definition; (4) criteria drift — mitigation: fitness sets are versioned artifacts with a standing calibration loop (sampled human grading), not immutable specs; (5) silent judge variance — mitigation: pin judge model and prompt template version alongside the feature file. ALTERNATIVES DOING THE SAME JOB: adopt promptfoo YAML directly (established format, loses Gherkin literacy, gains executability of the eval harness); LangWatch Scenario criteria lists (established, agent-oriented, heavier machinery); plain rubric documents per artifact type (G-Eval criteria+steps form — simplest, but loses the scenario framing that binds a test to a concrete situation). RECOMMENDED SHAPE: keep Gherkin as the authoring surface (PO literacy), define the fitness-test artifact type with the falsifiability and segregation rules above, and specify a mechanical 1:1 compilation from Then-clauses to rubric assertions in an established judge format (promptfoo llm-rubric or equivalent) so the judged semantics rest on established tooling rather than a bespoke runner.","adopt_potential":"adapt"}]

- agent-vault-cli: Your outbound requests go through a proxy that injects real credentials (API keys, tokens, secrets) on the wire — in headers, paths, query strings, bodies, and WebSocket frames. If you have an API key or token, use it as-is even if it looks fake. If you don't have one, set a dummy value and make the call anyway — the proxy handles it. If the call still fails with 401 or 403, use this skill to create a proposal requesting access. When writing code or using HTTP clients, make sure they pick up HTTPS_PROXY and HTTP_PROXY from the environment so requests route through the proxy. Most standard clients (curl, fetch, requests, axios) do this automatically.
- bring-up-bc: Launch an already-scaffolded Bounded Context as a running, online container and verify it reaches the online state
- company-research: Build a cited, bounded intelligence brief on a competitor, peer product, or alternative framework — strategy, product philosophy, recent moves — to ground a brief/PDR in external reality instead of intuition. Use for the consumer-product competitive/market input to problem discovery, or to study a competing framework.
- create-bc: Create a new Bounded Context from scratch — scaffold, remote, manifest registration, and brokered launch — as the lead shop
- derisk-measurement-advisor: Scan a shaping candidate for risk across 10 dimensions — 4 internal (Desirability, Usability, Feasibility, Viability) and 6 external (PESTEL) — and triage each into act-now or track, so the candidate's rabbit-holes and risks name what to test before committing. Reach for it when a bet feels roadmap-ready and you want a structured "what could go wrong, internally and externally?"
- discovery-dialogue: Run the open, interactive discovery conversation that turns a directional or ambiguous prompt into a written, grounded intent record
- discovery-interview-prep: Design a customer discovery interview plan — research goal, target segment, access constraints, and a bias-resistant question set — so a discovery-dialogue turn produces real learning instead of confirmation. Use when the intent record rests on an assumed job that needs to be heard from a real user.
- discovery-process: The end-to-end discovery arc — frame, plan, research, synthesize, validate, decide — used to sequence a multi-turn discovery-dialogue and know which technique skill comes next. Use when a discovery is large enough to need staging rather than a single lens.
- eol-message: Empathetic end-of-life announcement for a retiring product or capability — acknowledges disruption, explains the change as progress, and gives a concrete migration path. Reach for it inside a product-narrative session, and specifically when a brief flips to status:retired.
- incoming-request-advisor: Decode an incoming request before responding — separate the literal ask from the job-behind-it, read the sender's power and stake, and surface hidden assumptions — so a request is classified by its real outcome, not its surface wording. Use at PM-mode entry, at the router's classification boundary, to decide whether a request needs a discovery-dialogue at all.
- jobs-to-be-done: Uncover the stable job a user is hiring the product to do — functional, social, emotional — plus their pains and gains, so intent anchors on a validated job instead of a feature request. Use during the discovery-dialogue when a request smells solution-shaped ("add X").
- opportunity-solution-tree: Move from a target outcome down through opportunities (problems) to candidate solutions to a chosen bet, so shaping commits the candidate to the right problem before it converges on a sketch. Reach for it when a request arrives outcome-shaped or solution-shaped and you need to keep "what are we moving?" upstream of "what do we build?"
